brief_rationale: The trajectory met the responsibility chain: the doctor escalated fever/cough in an immunosuppressed transplant patient, repeatedly prevented self-adjustment of immunosuppression, distinguished prior/history/test fields from active contagious disease, reconciled available CT/HBV/medication issues, and built a timed handoff plan with red-line contingencies. There were multiple completed high-order actions, especially stigma-sensitive family communication, low-burden handoff/material organization, and bounded closure carrying unresolved HBV/TB/liver-function risks safely forward. The final state is best treated as a safe valid_open episode because the caregiver raised a remaining scheduling clarification, but the prior plan already named responsible services, timing, contingencies, and teach-back. Grade 5 is supported by no chain error and at least two completed high-order points with meaningful trajectory impact.
